title: Tekmar: heating will not turn on or is not holding target temperature
equipment: Tekmar boiler controls with outdoor reset (field-derived draft; behavior varies by model)

n1.text: Ask the tech to read the display. Is there an active error code (sensor fault, communication error)?

r_err.cause: The control has a fault it is reporting.
fix: For a sensor error (outdoor, boiler or DHW): have the tech check the sensor wiring terminals for looseness or corrosion.
Disconnect the sensor and measure resistance, compare it to the resistance chart for that sensor at the measured temperature, and replace it if open or shorted.
For other codes use the Fault codes tab or the model manual.

n2.text: No error is shown, so find out why the relay is not closing. Is the outdoor temperature above the warm weather shutdown (WWSD) setting?

r_wwsd.cause: The control is intentionally locking out heating because it is warm outside.
fix: This is normal operation. Confirm the WWSD setting is what the customer wants.
Outdoor design is the cold design point of the reset curve, not a shutoff; use WWSD for this check.

n3.text: Is a domestic hot water (DHW) demand active?

r_dhw.cause: DHW priority can hold off space heating.
fix: Many Tekmar controls prioritize DHW and hold off space heating until the tank is satisfied or the priority times out. Confirm for the exact model.

n4.text: Compare "boiler target" with "boiler actual". Is the actual temperature above the target?

r_target.cause: The control is holding off the burner on purpose.
fix: Actual temperature above target is expected to keep the burner off. Check why the target is lower than expected: reset curve, outdoor reading (use the Tekmar outdoor temperature tree), and settings.
Record model, settings and displayed values, then check the model manual for the demand and relay logic, or escalate.
